interest: This file provides an intriguing juxtaposition of U.S. State Department handling of Japanese cultural diplomacy immediately prior to World War II and post-war planning near the conflict's end. The 1940 documents illustrate the department's cautious navigation of Japan's 2,600th imperial anniversary essay contest organized by the Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai, balancing courtesy with wariness toward state-sponsored propaganda and currency restrictions on scholarship prize funds. In stark contrast, the 1944 memorandum highlights early interdivisional planning for the exploitation of enemy diplomatic and consular archives upon Japan's unconditional surrender, revealing bureaucratic tensions over staffing shortages and the European theater's priority over the Far East.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.414, 'History., Japan, Public Records.') covers State Department records between March 1940 and September 1944 relating to Japanese public records, cultural relations, and enemy archives. The earlier segment (March 1940) concerns an invitation from Matsuzo Nagai of the Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai (Society for International Cultural Relations) to promote a worldwide essay contest commemorating the 2,600th anniversary of the founding of the Japanese Empire. The Division of Cultural Relations and Division of Far Eastern Affairs coordinated a restrained response, noting that scholarship prize funds would need to be spent within Japan and advising that no action be taken beyond notifying the U.S. Consulate General in Tokyo. The later document (September 1944) addresses post-war planning by the Interdivisional Area Committee regarding the recruitment and training of personnel needed to seize, examine, and analyze the anticipated vast volume of Japanese diplomatic and consular files upon Japan's unconditional surrender, noting that preparations were lagging due to the prioritization of European operations.

subfiles.about: Memorandum concerning the need for adequate trained personnel to seize and examine Japanese diplomatic and consular files upon the unconditional surrender of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Walter Kahn writes to Abbot L. Moffat regarding discussions within the Interdivisional Area Committee on policy toward enemy consular and diplomatic files available after Japan's defeat. Kahn emphasizes that analyzing the immense volume of Japanese files will exceed current staff capacity unless personnel recruitment and training begin well in advance. Inquiries with Mr. Bechhoefer of the Office of Foreign Service revealed that European planning has absorbed most resources, leaving Far Eastern preparations behind, prompting Kahn to propose approaching the OSS upon Moffat's return.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Walter Kahn to Abbot L. Moffat on Staffing to Examine Enemy Files

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs offering no objection to acknowledging Matsuzo Nagai's letter regarding an essay contest.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Joseph W. Ballantine)
subfiles.summary: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs informs the Division of Cultural Relations that it sees no objection to acknowledging Matsuzo Nagai's letter and noting the enclosed pamphlet with interest. The note observes that, based on details on page 9 of the enclosure, the contest scholarship funds would need to be spent entirely within Japan. The memorandum reflects the Department's cautious approach to participating in Japanese-sponsored cultural ventures.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs regarding Acknowledgment of Matsuzo Nagai's Letter

subfiles.about: Memorandum requesting the views of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs on participating in the 26th Centennial International Essay Contest of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Charles A. Thomson of the Division of Cultural Relations queries the Division of Far Eastern Affairs regarding an attached letter from the organizers of the 26th Centennial International Essay Contest of Japan. Thomson asks whether FE considers it desirable or wise to accede to the organizers' request and cooperate to the modest extent requested. Departmental stamps record receipt by FE on March 20, 1940, and further handling by Cultural Relations in April 1940.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Charles A. Thomson to Division of Far Eastern Affairs regarding Essay Contest Inquiry

subfiles.about: Letter from the Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai inviting U.S. participation and publicity for an international essay contest commemorating the 2,600th anniversary of the Japanese Empire.
subfiles.summary: Matsuzo Nagai, Chairman of the Contest Committee of Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai, writes to Ben Cherrington announcing a worldwide prize essay contest celebrating the 2,600th anniversary of the founding of the Empire of Japan. Nagai requests Cherrington's support in circulating information about the contest among colleagues and potential contestants. The letter expresses the hope that the initiative will foster a broader appreciation of Japanese culture abroad and strengthen international cultural relations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Matsuzo Nagai to Ben Cherrington Announcing the 26th Centennial International Essay Contest

subfiles.about: Memorandum advising that no action be taken on the Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai letter beyond sending an instruction to the U.S. Consulate General in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Maxwell M. Hamilton / Cabot Coville)
subfiles.summary: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs advises the Division of Cultural Relations regarding the February 2, 1940 letter from Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai. FE recommends that no action is necessary other than transmitting an attached instruction to the American Consulate General in Tokyo. This concluded the Department's internal review by opting for minimal formal involvement in the Japanese cultural celebration.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs to Division of Cultural Relations regarding Action on Essay Contest Letter
